title: Vanishing of H_1 and of the differentials at a prime gives an etale localization
statement: Let $A\to C$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings making $C$ a finitely presented $A$-algebra, and $\mathfrak q\subset C$ a prime ideal such that the localizations at $\mathfrak q$ of the $C$-modules $H_1(L_{C/A})$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and $\Omega_{C/A}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] vanish: $H_1(L_{C/A})_{\mathfrak q}=0$ and $(\Omega_{C/A})_{\mathfrak q}=0$. Then there is $h\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $\operatorname{Spec}C_h\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, induced by $A\to C\to C_h$, is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07BU (lemma-smooth-at-point, line 37523), (2)=>(1) with Omega_{C/A,q} = 0 free of rank 0, Definition Tag 00TB (definition-smooth-at-prime: smooth at q = C_h smooth for some h not in q), Definition Tag 00U1 (definition-etale, line 39245: etale = finitely presented with NL quasi-isomorphic to 0, etale at q likewise); comparison with etale morphisms of schemes by literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex Lemma Tag 02GJ (lemma-etale-characterize); used in More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 07M7 ('By Algebra, Lemma 07BU we see that A -> C is smooth at the prime q-bar ... Since Omega_{C/A,q} = 0 it is actually etale at q-bar')
